output.title: Rounding claims in a one-person business
output.body:
If you run a one-person business, the real question is not whether AI can “handle claims.” It is whether the rounding work is repetitive enough to become a bounded workflow instead of a string of fresh judgment calls.

Use a simple rule: keep it manual when each case needs new context or exceptions; consider support only when the same checks repeat. In a claims workflow, AI can sort, compare, or flag items before you review them. Final approval stays with you. That is the control boundary. Human-only approval and refusal of agent approval are demonstrated only in Bareni’s self-built accounts-payable demo on synthetic data; for claims rounding, this is a design rule, not a deployed system.

The practical next step is to map one week of the current process. Write down the trigger, inputs, decision rule, where rounding happens, and where you stop to check by hand. Then mark the parts that are actually repeatable. If the rule can be written clearly, it may be a candidate for support. If it depends on judgment every time, manual review is still the right default.

That is usually the useful filter: not “Can AI do it?” but “Which part is stable enough to standardise without giving up owner control?”
